issues.description: Negated typeof check complects two questions into one expression
issues.detail: The condition `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` complects 'is this a layer' with 'does it have a block' inside a longer boolean chain. The underlying fact is simple: a layer statement (no block) is allowed before @import; a layer block is not. A small helper like `isLayerStatement(node)` (returns true when name is 'layer' and `node.nodes` is undefined) would let the predicate read as a list of allowed forms rather than a negated conjunction, separating the 'what kind of node is this' value from the 'is it allowed here' decision.

issues.description: `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` leans on a PostCSS implementation detail rather than a named concept
issues.detail: Whether an at-rule is a 'statement' (semicolon-terminated) or a 'block' (has a body) is a real fact about the value. The code expresses it via `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'`, which is easy (familiar JS idiom) but not simple — it ties the rule to PostCSS's internal representation of empty vs. missing `nodes`. PostCSS exposes this distinction more directly (e.g. checking for a block via the presence of `nodes` as an array). Naming the concept once (`hasBlock(node)` or `isStatementAtRule(node)`) makes the value explicit and survives PostCSS refactors.

issues.description: Test coverage misses the layer-with-block-and-content and layer-statement-list cases
issues.detail: The added test covers `@layer foo {}` before `@import`. The values in play are: layer-statement (`@layer foo;` or `@layer foo, bar;`) which should remain allowed, and layer-block (`@layer foo { ... }`) which should be rejected. Only an empty block is exercised in the new reject test. A test asserting that `@layer foo, bar;` followed by `@import` still passes, and one for `@layer foo { .a {} }` (non-empty block) failing, would pin the value distinction this PR actually depends on.

review.summary: The fix is correct and minimal: it distinguishes a layer statement (allowed before @import per spec) from a layer block (not allowed), which is the right factual decomposition. The complecting is small but real — the predicate inlines a negated conjunction and reaches into PostCSS's `node.nodes` representation rather than naming the concept of 'statement vs. block at-rule.' A tiny helper would make the values explicit and the allowed-forms list read as a list rather than a chain of negations. Test coverage should also pin both sides of the value distinction (layer-statement-list still allowed; layer-block with content rejected), not just the empty-block case. SIMPLE-enough to ship; the cleanup is a P2 readability and future-proofing nit, not a blocker.
